spec: PLAYBACK-DESIGN §4, §8, §13 item 8. The event pump against the full §4 mapping and the DUR table of §8. Every event either has a beat or is explicitly silent-but-logged; there is no third category. THE SPLIT SWING is the hard part and the reason the naive one-event-one-beat mapping is wrong: a projectile takes ~700ms, so the travel half plays on attack.declared/attack.hit and the impact half is HELD until damage.applied — otherwise the bolt lands on a target that already took the damage. attack.hit is DUR 0 on purpose: its beat is a Promise that resolves when the projectile lands, and the pump awaits that, not a number. The speed multiplier scales durations uniformly and must never scale ORDER — at x4 the split swing must still split.
expect: all 37 event types are handled, damage never lands before its projectile at any speed multiplier, and an unknown event type logs a finding line and continues rather than stopping an otherwise honest replay

spec: bestAttack() takes the FIRST affordable attack in the unit's declared order, so an authored kit's later entries are dead unless the first is unaffordable. Surfaced by content.alpha-flip (2026-09-02) — in 200 standard battles the Alpha Sky Pirate never threw the Javelin (its melee-aggressive mode closes to reach 1, where a ranged attack is illegal) and never drew the Dagger (javelin.stab precedes it, same cost); Osric never used Longsword Stab (+2, cost 2) or Shield Slam (stun rider) because Slash (+1, cost 1) is first and affordable. The test cohort hid this: its kits were ordered dear-first. AMBIGUITY, NOT A DECISION: the choice policy is a SWITCH (declared-order | best-preview-damage | best-preview-with-riders) with declared-order as the default it has always been, and a sweep answers which policy the AI should use. Riders (a self-Protection on the dagger, a stun on the slam) are not priced by preview() at all — that is the third policy's question. ALSO: the Sky Pirate's role is 'ranged' in the pack while its ai is 'melee-aggressive' — a converter/derivation question for the content chat, noted here so it is not lost.
expect: with the switch at best-preview the four dead attacks fire in the standard battle and integration.test's exact dead-list shrinks to []; with declared-order it stays as asserted; the effect of each policy on the eight control battles is measured by a sweep, not decided
generalizationExempt: a SWITCH on the AI's choice rule, not a content mechanism: there is no row to vary — the two policies are the two code paths, and the sweep is the instrument

The row flag is data (shedByHealing: 'half'); the base of the shed is a SWITCH (bleedShedFromLanded: the hp that actually landed vs the post-Burn amount asked, which differ only at full health).

spec: The engine reads its status rows from the Codex. Andrew 2026-09-02, asked whether the Codex may own the rows: 'Yes — Codex owns the rows.' content/mkenginepack.mjs compiles each settled.json status row's ONE SENTENCE into the engine's behaviour flags by EXACT phrase (compile-or-name-the-gap: a row the engine cannot behave for is not emitted, it is a named gap, and every trigger or chart clause naming it becomes a gap too); the pack carries a statuses section; the loader (packStatuses) validates it loudly and turns `tick` into the End-of-Phase hook — the one place a row becomes a function. src/content/statuses.ts keeps ONLY the test.* lane and refuses a hand-typed status.* row.
